$comment: Thresholds for the committed k6 scenario in performance/smoke.js.
`release` holds the k6 threshold expressions verbatim. That is deliberately
not a set of numbers with a separate operator field: the previous shape
recorded bare numbers and `scripts/performance-gate.mjs` reconstructed the
expression from them, so only p95, p99 and the failure rate were ever
cross-checked. `checks.rate` sat in the record at 1 while the scenario said
`rate>0.99` and nothing compared them — a threshold that had drifted and a
gate that could not see it, which is the same defect as no gate.
With the expressions recorded, the cross-check is a substring test over the
whole set: a scenario that relaxes or tightens any threshold without the
record changing fails the gate, and so does a record edited alone.
These are the floors for a self-hosted single-node install on the reference
hardware, not a service-level agreement. They exist to catch a regression
that a change to this repository introduced, which is the only claim the CI
gate can make.
**Tightened on 2026-10-21 from `p(95)<500` / `p(99)<1500` to the values below, after
the first recorded run.** The old numbers were estimates written before anything was
measured, at ~90x and ~240x the observed latency — a p95 of 400 ms would have passed
them. The new ceilings keep roughly 9x headroom over the slowest p95 observed on either
host (5.47 ms on the reference install; 2.09–3.21 ms across six nightly runs on
ubuntu-24.04, which is where the gate actually runs) and ~24x over the observed p99, so
scheduler noise does not fail the nightly while an order-of-magnitude regression does.

observed_on_reference_hardware.$comment: Recorded by `pnpm test:performance` on the reference install, read from `var/performance-summary.json`. Not a gate: the `release` block is.
observed_on_reference_hardware.hardware: Self-hosted single node: Intel Core i7-13650HX (14 cores / 20 threads), 31.7 GB RAM, Windows 11 Pro; PostgreSQL 16 (postgres:16-alpine) in Docker Desktop; API started by scripts/performance-server.mjs exactly as nightly.yml starts it; k6 v2.2.0.
observed_on_reference_hardware.reason: Two consecutive runs of the committed scenario agreed to within 2% (p95 5.39 / 5.47 ms, p99 6.20 / 6.32 ms). The second is recorded. 8049 requests, 0 failed, every check passed. 41 iterations were dropped by k6 at the 50 iterations/s peak because `maxVUs: 50` is exactly the peak rate with a 1 s sleep per iteration; the nightly runs drop the same number, so the scenario is reproducible as committed and was not changed to hide it.

endpoints_deliberately_not_covered: /api/v1/events (SSE — a long-lived stream, not a latency budget)
/api/v1/reporter/upload (multipart, covered by a body-size limit instead)
